# dsh-skill-workspace
English | 中文
Keep every skill in one **configurable directory**, and let **each workspace decide** which of them
skill in one **configurable directory**, and let **each workspace decide** which of them it may use.
Two entry points, two jobs:
| Where | What it controls |

| **Settings → Skills** | The skills directory (defaults to `~/.dsh/skills`) |
| **The ✦ icon in the
chat title bar** | Which skills the current workspace enables (checkboxes) |
## Why this exists

DSH's built-in `skill-filesystem` has a fixed user root at `~/.dsh/skills`, and it treats
every sess

ion the same way: either all skills are visible (and cost context) or none are.
Once you have a few
of them, every session pays for skills it will never use.

This plugin does not touch the built-in scanner. It registers its own provider and, for each
skill i
n the directory, returns a **candidate under the same name**:

- the workspace **has it checked** → a normal candidate; `get()` reads the body;
- **not checked** →
a same-name candidate whose `modelInvocable` / `userInvocable` are both `false`.

The registry merges by "same-layer duplicates are decided by rank, while **a nearer layer
overrides

a farther one outright**", and the invocation policy travels with the winning
entry. An unchecked sk

ill therefore **really disappears** from the model catalog, and
`/name` cannot reach it either.
### ⚠️ The catch: the provider has to be registered twice

The built-in `skill-filesystem` is mounted **inside each agent preset**, so its candidates
land in t

he **preset's scope layer**. Registering only in the global layer means the preset
layer overrides u
s — and this is not theory, it is what testing showed:

1. Register in the global layer only, with rank `350` (ahead of the built-in user root at
`400`), th

en drop a skill into `~/.dsh/skills` → **it still shows up in the session
catalog** (rank only decid

es within one layer; across layers it is irrelevant).
2. Also register on **`agent.ctx`** from `agen

t/created` (an agent's own layer is nearer
than the preset's), same skill → **it disappears**.
3. Ch
eck that skill for the current workspace → **it comes back**.

So `apply()` registers twice: once globally (a fallback for scopes with no nearer provider)
and once

per agent (the one that actually beats the preset layer). Registrations on an
agent's scope are not

released when the plugin unloads, so `releaseAll()` tears them all down
on unload or hot reload, le
aving no provider pointing at a dead service.

Project-level skills (`<workspace>/.dsh/skills`, rank 100) sit on the same layer chain but
from a di

fferent source: they are **never affected by the checkboxes and stay always
available**. This plugin
governs the skill library directory only.
## Storage
`$DSH_HOME/storages/skill_workspace_policy.json`
[代码示例省略，未执行]

**No entry for a workspace means nothing is selected there.** That is a product decision,
matching t
he MCP policy, not missing data: an unchecked skill must not cost context.

> ⚠️ Editing this file by hand does not take effect immediately (the host reads it once when
> the p

lugin loads, keeps it in memory afterwards, and does not watch the file). Checking
> boxes in the UI

**is** immediate: write to disk → `invalidate()` → the catalog refreshes on
> the next turn.
## When changes take effect

- **Checking a box**: the skill registry is invalidated right away, so sessions in that
workspace se

e the new catalog on their **next turn**. The turn already in flight does not
change (the catalog is

taken at `agent/pre-step`).
- **Changing the directory**: same as above. A missing directory is cre

ated with `mkdir -p`.
- Neither requires a restart or a remount.
## Directory layout and file format

Exactly **one level** is scanned: `<dir>/<name>/SKILL.md` or `<dir>/<name>.md`. Nested
`**/SKILL.md`
files are deliberately not supported (same as the built-in provider).
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- `name` is required and must be kebab-case;
- `description` is required — **it is the only thing th

e model routes on**;
- optional `whenToUse`, `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable` (booleans

accept
`true/false`, `yes/no`, `on/off`, `1/0`).

Malformed files (missing frontmatter, bad name, misspelled boolean) are **collected and listed
in th
e UI** rather than skipped silently the way the built-in scanner skips them.
## Remote API

The client calls these through `ctx.remote.skillWorkspace` (hand-written remote descriptors,
followi
ng `dsh-mcp-workspace-policy`):
| Method | Input | Returns |
| `list` | `{}` | `{ dir, defaultDir, missing, skills, errors, shadowed, byWorkspace, storePath, rec

entErrors }` |
| `set` | `{ workspace, selected }` | `{ applied, workspace, selected, unknown, persi

sted }` |
| `setDir` | `{ dir }` (empty string restores the default) | `{ applied, dir, created, per
`setDir` | `{ dir }` (empty string restores the default) | `{ applied, dir, created, persisted }` |
## Development

No dependencies, no build step. The host half is plain ESM; the client half is a
`window.__ModuleLoa

, no build step. The host half is plain ESM; the client half is a
`window.__ModuleLoader__` factory.

## Changelog

- 2026-10-26 First implementation: configurable directory plus per-workspace checkboxes.
The title-b

ar MCP button was turned into an icon in the same pass (that change lives in
`dsh-split-workspaces`:

`client.skill.js`, `client.pane.js`, `client.menu.js`).
- 2026-10-26 The SKILL popover now reloads

its list **every time it opens**; previously it
only reloaded when its state was unhealthy, so a dir

ectory changed in Settings did not show
up until the page was refreshed.
